properties.statement:
ONE WORKFLOW, SEVEN SPELLINGS OF 'WHICH NODE', AND FOUR DIFFERENT STATUS CONTRACTS ACROSS SIBLING CONSTRUCTORS. Reported by dev_storyflow across two entries on 2026-09-02, after five failed calls before any of a brainstorm's writes landed — all parameter-shape errors, none conceptual.

THE SPELLINGS, their table: `search_design` RETURNS `node_id`+`node_type`; `get_node` takes `id`+`node_type`; `create_node` takes `id`+`node_type`+nested `props`; `review_relations` takes `node_id`+`node_type` and `other_id`/`other_type`; `authored_by` takes `from_id`+`from_type`; `schedule_for` takes `item_id`+`item_type`; `set_epoch_status` takes `epoch_id`; `verifies` adds `verification_id`.

⭐ THE SIGNATURE THEY NAME IS THE DAMNING PART: 'search_design hands back `node_id`; the tool you reach for next rejects that exact key... EVERY GUESS WAS INFORMED BY THE TOOL I HAD USED IMMEDIATELY BEFORE, AND EVERY ONE WAS WRONG' — which is the signature of an interface that is LOCALLY SENSIBLE AND GLOBALLY INCONSISTENT rather than of a careless caller.

SHARPEST SINGLE CASE: `add_epoch` takes `id` and `set_epoch_status` takes `epoch_id`. Two tools, one node type, adjacent in every workflow.

⭐⭐ CORROBORATED FIRST-HAND 2026-09-04, WITHOUT LOOKING FOR IT. Cutting v0.47.1 this session, the release procedure called `add_epoch(id: "epoch:v0471-cut")` and then `set_epoch_status(epoch_id: ...)` — exactly the pair they name — and `add_epoch` returned `status: "arrived"` UNASKED. Both halves of their report reproduced in an unrelated workflow by an agent that had not yet read it.

THE STATUS CONTRACTS, their table: `add_decision` lands `proposed` (correct, and the brainstorm skill tells you to VERIFY it); `add_capability` accepts and honours an explicit `status`; `add_epoch` lands `arrived` — work that has not started recorded as already happened; `add_verification` REJECTS the field outright and lands `planned`, so recording a check that FAILED takes two calls and forgetting the second leaves a failing check reading `planned`.

⚠️ THE `add_epoch` DEFAULT IS DEFENSIBLE AND THE SILENCE IS NOT. `plan_epoch` exists for epochs that have NOT happened, and `add_epoch`'s own description says it is for one that HAS — so the default is coherent. Their complaint survives that: nothing in the REPLY says which status was chosen, and they created two epochs for unstarted work and caught it only by reading the response. Their proposed remedy is the brainstorm skill's own rule generalised — echo the status actually assigned.

THEIR WISH LIST, verbatim in intent: one addressing convention (`node_id`+`node_type` everywhere, with `id`/`from_id` accepted as ALIASES); `get_node`'s error should say `and` not `or` (it reads as either/or, so the obvious correction fails a second time — two round trips for one call); one status contract, defaulting to the not-yet-done end and echoing what was assigned; typed constructors should reach every field the node type has (`add_epoch` rejects `description`).

🛑 THIS IS A BREAKING SURFACE CHANGE AND IS NOT RECOMMENDED HERE. Aliases are additive and cheap; renaming is not. Recorded as a measured friction with a first-hand reproduction, for the user to rule on.
